text:
alex: quick idea — can we introduce a "compact sampling" mode for config rollouts? basically keep full rollout behavior but only emit a tiny telemetry payload for X% of requests so we cut ingestion during big experiments.

maria: by "tiny payload" you mean aggregated counters only? worried about losing request-level signals for regressions. :thinking_face:

jc: maybe we do a dual-path: sampled requests (full telemetry + traces) versus compact requests (only cohort id, outcome bool, short latency bucket). that way evals still work for sampled set.

alex: exactly. goal is reduce raw event volume while keeping enough fidelity to detect major regressions. want to experiment at 1%, 5%, 20% during rollouts. also could tie to user cohorts.

priya: API question — how would this look in the runtime config schema? need a clear semantics for sampling so router + runtime know when to emit compact vs full.

alex: sketch:```json
{
  "flag": "new-routing-v2",
  "rollout": {
    "cohorts": ["stable","canary"],
    "compact_sampling": {
      "percent": 5,
      "scope": "cohort",
      "seed_key": "user_id",
      "min_full_samples_per_min": 10
    }
  }
}
```

sam: console/UX thought — slider for percent + an optional per-cohort override. show an estimated events/s reduction and projected cost delta. also a warning if compact_sampling would make detection latency > X mins.

maria: how do we handle quota enforcement and billing traces? if we stop sending full events, downstream billing pipelines might undercount tokens, etc. need to be careful.

jc: billing should still count tokens at ingress; compact sampling only affects telemetry emitted to observability (events/metrics). we need separation in docs and telemetry pipelines.

alex: good point — add explicit fields: "telemetry_target":"observability" vs "billing". default: compact sampling only affects observability.

ops-bot: deploy-trigger: rollout-config updated by alex — diff looks safe. CI checks: config-schema passed, unit tests passed. :rocket:

priya: edge-case — what if a compact-sampled cohort has a small absolute qps (e.g., 2 r/s)? percent-based sampling could starve full samples. we should support absolute floor: min_full_samples_per_min (see example).

sam: UX: show when floors kick in and estimate how many full samples we'll get per hour per cohort. also add a toggle to force 100% full telemetry for a short window if incident is detected.

maria: alerting change — any regression alert should automatically escalate to a forced full-sample window for at least 5 minutes so we can triage. add as a server-side policy.

jc: implementation notes: router needs deterministic sampling (seed_key hashed) so we maintain per-user consistency during a rollout. runtime SDK should expose: is_full_sampled(request) and telemetry_format(request).

alex: agree. steps: 1) spec + schema PR, 2) runtime SDK change (is_full_sampled API), 3) console UX mock + telemetry estimates, 4) small canary rollout 5% on internal org, collect evals.

priya: I'll own schema PR. sam you ok to mock the console cards? jc can you do runtime prototype?

sam: yep I'll do UX mock by EOD Thursday.

jc: can prototype in runtime branch, will include deterministic RNG and min_full_samples_per_min enforcement.

alex: thanks. one more: add a telemetry gate so compact mode is auto-disabled if certain error rates spike (e.g., 5xx rate or latency p95 > threshold). we don't want blind spots.

maria: +1 to auto-disable on spillover. also log when auto-disable happened and which cohorts were affected.

alex: ok putting these action items in the PR description. thanks all. :raised_hands:

ops-bot: note: follow-up meeting scheduled in #eng-platform for 2026-03-23 10:00 UTC to review UX + schema.
